consolidated.src: q1fy27Ppt (consolidated table, Rs mn converted); Screener

call: Consolidated price growth ~5% in Q1 ('4% to 5%. About 5%'); Q2 to add ~3% in decorative and 3-5% in industrial as price rises flow through.

Decorative value growth high single digit; decorative volume growth low single digit (mix: economy grew mid single digit, super-premium double digit). Industrial grew double digit: auto, powder and performance-coating liquids strong; auto refinish flat.
Competitive intensity 'continues to remain intact'; 'for this year, at least that intensity will remain'; no change in pricing discipline or dealer incentives vs last year.

FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13-14% maintained ('our endeavour is to maintain 13% to 14%'); medium-term aim 'higher end of 14% plus' in 2-3 years; Q2 margin to be held vs Q2FY26 despite high-cost inventory.

Rs601 cr capex for automotive, powder and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur: +65,880 KL/yr paint and powder and +9,780 KL/yr resin, over ~2-2.5 years, on top of normal capex of Rs150-200 cr; expected ROCE in line with current, 'towards 18%' later; industrial utilisation 70-75%.
Aim to become No.1 in industrial (non-auto) in about two years; in decorative 'maintain our position, if not improve'.
Network expansion of 5-10% a year; 1,700+ dealers added in Q1; ad spend raised in Q1.

rawMaterials.summary: West Asia conflict from late Feb-2026: crude oil and solvents surged, the rupee hit record lows (~95.2/US$ on 30-Apr-2026, when Brent touched ~US$120), supply chains were disrupted. KNPL raised decorative prices four times (25-Mar 2%, then 10-Apr, 21-Apr and 11-May at 5-6% each, 'higher single digit' net); industrial price rises lag 1-2 quarters. Management said crude at ~US$100 needs no further price rise; input prices eased from the June peak. Raw materials are 55-60% of sales (CRISIL).

history.event: Founded in Mumbai as Gahagan Paints & Varnish; later renamed Goodlass Nerolac Paints.
Technical collaboration with Kansai Paint and Nihon Tokushu Toryo of Japan; Kansai Paint later took control (74.96% today).
Nerofix JV with Polygel (60%) for adhesives and construction chemicals; Marpol and Perma Construction Aids merged into KNPL (accounts recast from FY21): the base of the Perma waterproofing range.
1:2 bonus issue (shares 53.9 cr to 80.9 cr). Sale of the Kavesar (Thane) property: Rs661 cr pre-tax gain; Rs1.25 special dividend. Birla Opus (Grasim) launches in Feb-2024.

Sale of the Lower Parel (Mumbai) factory land and building: Rs665 cr gain; Rs186 cr impairment of Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (standalone); Rs1.25 special dividend. Kansai Paint's first India strategy briefing (18-Apr-2025).
Pravin Chaudhari succeeds Anuj Jain as MD; CFO P. D. Pai retires (Jul-2025), Yash Ahuja takes over.
JSW Paints agrees to buy up to 74.76% of Akzo Nobel India (Dulux) for up to Rs8,986 cr (Jun-2025) and completes the purchase of 60.76% from Akzo Nobel in Dec-2025.
60% of Kansai Paints Lanka sold to Atire (Pvt) Ltd for LKR 1.8 mn (~Rs5 lakh).

Exceptional charges Rs63 cr (Wage Code Rs45 cr, Ghaziabad warehouse fire Rs13 cr, Bangladesh impairment Rs6 cr). Nerofix amalgamation approved by shareholders (27-Feb-2026), appointed date 1-Apr-2025.

Kansai Paint's second India strategy briefing: decorative to be run for stability in focused markets; growth from auto and industrial; +200bp margin aim; divesting decorative 'not a call we would like to take'.
Rs601 cr capex approved for automotive, powder and resin capacity (Sayakha, Bawal, Hosur).
